GenerateMonsters.note: C# draws THREE times: NextItem on the 2-item _smallSlimes list picks small A; the pick is removed, leaving one item, and NextItem is called AGAIN on that 1-item list (a forced but still RNG-consuming pick, small B); then NextItem(_mediumSlimes) picks the medium. Return order is [A, medium, B] (positions 0/1/2), so the draw ORDER (small,small,medium) differs from the RETURN order (small,medium,small). The sim's parity branch reproduces every part of this exactly: selection_rng.next_item(smalls) -> remove -> selection_rng.next_item(smalls) (still consumes a draw on the 1-item remainder) -> selection_rng.next_item([LeafSlimeM, TwigSlimeM]) -> returns [small_a, medium, small_b]. Executed witness (seed 12345): roster=['LeafSlimeS','TwigSlimeM','TwigSlimeS'], draws=3 -- always both small types plus one random medium, 3 draws, matching the C# shape including the forced-but-counted second draw. See the guards entry below for the non-parity (legacy) path.

guards.what: Encounter Rng independence outside parity (default/legacy) mode
guards.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). `RunState.create_combat` now builds the per-encounter Rng on BOTH paths: with a string seed from `rng_set.seed` as before, and without one from a run seed derived at construction (`run.derive_encounter_seed`, a hash of the shared generator's STATE, so it consumes no draw and shifts no other legacy stream). `create_monsters`' `selection_rng=None` arm is therefore unreachable from any production call site, and the composition no longer moves when the shared stream does — executed in test/test_encounter_selection_rng.py (test_the_composition_does_not_move_with_the_shared_stream) and by audit/tools/encounter_probes_e2.py legacy-shared-stream.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: Same mechanism as ruby_raiders' guard (full rationale there). With no string seed, SlimesWeakEncounter.create_monsters falls back to `rng.sample([LeafSlimeS, TwigSlimeS], 2)` + `rng.choice([LeafSlimeM, TwigSlimeM])` on the shared combat_rng.legacy() stream. Executed witness: py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e2.py legacy-shared-stream confirms the shared-object identity for CombatState(encounter=SLIMES_WEAK). Does not explain the 89U conformance divergence (89U's replay takes the correct parity branch, verdicted faithful above); this is a 3-act seed anyway (Ironclad) and slimes_weak is act-1 content, so it is directly in scope for that seed's early floors, but only via the legacy path, which conformance runs never take.
